 > How to: Setup Icons on a Grid
Adding a conditional statement in the COLUMN_TEMPLATE column of the SCREEN_CONTROL_GRID_COLUMNS table will provide a conditional icon displayed on the grid column when the conditions are met.

To setup an icon on a grid, we first need to add a conditional statement into the COLUMN_TEMPLATE column. This conditional statement will be defined using the handlebar format and  will be stored in SCREEN_CONTROL_GRID_COLUMNS table. The condition will be checked when the datagrid is rendered. When the condition is satisfied, the icon defined in the conditional statement will be displayed for each row meeting the condition.
Font awesome will be the icon framework used. For a list of icons see

Below is the screenshot showing the contents of SCREEN_CONTROL_GRID_COLUMNS table in which a conditional statement is added. The conditional statement in this screenshot is defined as: If the permanent column of the grid is 'Y', then the icon will be displayed on grid column.
Step 1: Determine the Object Id for the screen control - ListPaneDataGrid

Use the following SQL to determine the Object Id for the screen control name ListPaneDataGrid if you know the Form Id. The below example illustrates this to determine the Object Id for the scren control name ListPaneDataGrid if you know the form id represented as <form id> below. Insight Architect can also be used for this (
How to: Use Insight Architect to Customize a Metadata Page
Find the Object Id for screen control

Use the following SQL to update the value in the handlebar format. Update the column_template column in the SCREEN_CONTROL_GRID_COLUMNS table. The below example illustrates this for an insight listpane data grid. Insight Architect can also be used for this (
How to: Use Insight Architect to Customize a Metadata Page
As a result of this SQL statement,icon would be displayed on the grid column for grid rows that are assigned to Permanent = Y.
For specific information on handlebars refer the following article:
NOTE: %20 must be used for spaces for example CARRIER === UPS%20GROUND
The column of the grid used in conditional statement is case sensitive.
To determine the column value needed for a conditional statement, refer to the associated value found in the FIELD_NAME column of the SCREEN_GROUP_COLUMN table for the corresponding grid.
The below example illustrates this for a shipment header details grid.
The below examples depict the occurance of multiple conditions.
Icon with muliple condition using AND
The above example can be written in the handlebar format as
'{{#ifCond WAREHOUSE ''=='' ''MN''}}{{#ifCond INVENTORY_STS ''=='' ''Available''}}<}}{{/ifCond}}{{/ifCond}}'
Icon with muliple condition using OR
The above example can be written in the handlebar format as
'{{#ifCond WAREHOUSE ''=='' ''MN''}}<Row-Color bg=''blue'' fg=''white'' />{{/ifCond}}{{#ifCond INVENTORY_STS ''=='' ''Available''}}<Row-Color bg=''blue'' fg=''white'' />{{/ifCond}}'
Refresh the Insight screen to apply these changes

This conditional statement will be defined using the handlebar format and  will be stored in SCREEN_CONTROL_GRID_COLUMNS table. The condition will be checked when the datagrid is rendered. When the condition is satisfied, the icon defined in the conditional statement will be displayed for each row meeting the condition.   Font awesome will be the icon framework used. For a list of icons see https://fontawesome.com/icons?d=gallery. Below is the screenshot showing the contents of SCREEN_CONTROL_GRID_COLUMNS table in which a conditional statement is added. The conditional statement in this screenshot is defined as: If the permanent column of the grid is 'Y', then the icon will be displayed on grid column.      Step 1: Determine the Object Id for the screen control - ListPaneDataGrid Use the following SQL to determine the Object Id for the screen control name ListPaneDataGrid if you know the Form Id. The below example illustrates this to determine the Object Id for the scren control name ListPaneDataGrid if you know the form id represented as
below. Insight Architect can also be used for this (How to: Use Insight Architect to Customize a Metadata Page). Find the Object Id for screen control Copy Code SELECT OBJECT_ID FROM SCREEN_CONTROL WHERE SCREEN_GROUP_ID IN (SELECT OBJECT_ID FROM SCREEN_GROUP WHERE SCREEN_PART_ID IN (SELECT OBJECT_ID FROM SCREEN_PART WHERE SCREEN_ID IN (SELECT OBJECT_ID FROM MAIN_UI_SCREEN WHERE FORM_ID=) AND PART_NAME='LISTPANE') AND GROUP_NAME='LISTPANEPANEL')  Step 2: Update the value in Column_Template Use the following SQL to update the value in the handlebar format. Update the column_template column in the SCREEN_CONTROL_GRID_COLUMNS table. The below example illustrates this for an insight listpane data grid. Insight Architect can also be used for this (How to: Use Insight Architect to Customize a Metadata Page). Update the  Column_Template Copy Code UPDATE SCREEN_CONTROL_GRID_COLUMNS SET COLUMN_TEMPLATE='{{#ifCond Permanent '==' 'Y'}}{{/ifCond}}' where SCREEN_CONTROL_ID=

rows.text: Find the Object Id for screen control

SELECT OBJECT_ID FROM SCREEN_CONTROL WHERE SCREEN_GROUP_ID IN
                (SELECT OBJECT_ID FROM SCREEN_GROUP WHERE SCREEN_PART_ID IN  
                    (SELECT OBJECT_ID FROM SCREEN_PART WHERE SCREEN_ID IN
                        (SELECT OBJECT_ID FROM MAIN_UI_SCREEN WHERE FORM_ID=<form id>) AND PART_NAME='LISTPANE')
                             AND GROUP_NAME='LISTPANEPANEL')
